newsitem.title: USA: Non-profit group sues over abortion pill.
newsitem.headline: Non-profit group sues over abortion pill.

text.p: A non-profit group that holds the U.S. patent rights to the French abortion pill RU-486 said on Monday it had sued the businessman who holds sub-licenses to develop the pill, accusing him of fraud and seeking to force him to sell his interests.

The New York-based Population Council said it filed the lawsuit against Joseph Pike, who controls companies holding sub-licenses for the manufacture and distribution of the abortion-inducing drug mifepristone.

The council, which holds U.S. patent rights to the drug, sub-licensed them to Pike's companies but learned in July that he was "not an appropriate person" to be involved in its introduction to the U.S. market, said council spokeswoman Sandra Waldman.
The council gave Pike until noon on Monday to sell his interests and he failed to meet the deadline, she said.
Pike was accused in a lawsuit filed last week in Los Angeles by KCC Delaware, a subsidiary of Beverly Hills, California-based Giant Group Ltd., of using the venture as an illegal money-making scheme.

KCC said it invested $6 million with Pike under the assumption it would own 26 percent of a firm to manufacture and distribute the drug. But KCC claimed Pike sold similar stakes to other investors and tried to sell equity interests that combined would total more than 100 percent.
KCC said it learned Pike was a disbarred attorney who had pleaded guilty to forgery in a fraudulent real estate scheme and had been given a two-year suspended prison sentence.
The Population Council sued Pike for fraud, Waldman said. "He concealed crucial facts bearing directly on his character and fitness for a leading role in the project," she said.
The lawsuit seeks unspecified damages and a court order to force him to sell his interests, she said.
The legal disputes could delay the introduction of the pill in the United States, Waldman said last week. However, its development for the U.S. market will proceed, she said.

The French company Roussel Uclaf, a unit of Hoechst AG F, donated the drug's U.S. patent rights to the council, which set up a company called Advances in Health Technology Inc. in Washington to market it.
Pike was the principal of San Diego-based Neogen Investors LP and a group of affiliated companies which holds the U.S. license for mifepristone as an abortion-inducing drug.

In a related development, Neogen Corp. of Lansing, Michigan, issued a statement saying it was in no way related to Neogen Investors LP and it was considering legal action to stop the San Diego company from using the Neogen name.
On Friday, Reuters erroneously included Neogen Corp.'s stock symbol in a reference to KCC's legal case against Pike.

The Food and Drug Administration recently ruled the abortion drug, which has been used for years throughout much of Europe, was safe and effective. It is expected to approve it for use in the United States sometime next year.
